title: Aegis Biosys - Pen Test Remediation & Patch Sprint Planning
next_steps: Redwood to share the annotated pen-test findings spreadsheet (Maya) by 2025-07-24
Customer to confirm which issues will be accepted vs remediated by 2025-07-31
Schedule 60-min follow-up to review patch sprint plan for 2025-08-05
Redwood to provide temporary mitigation playbook for high-risk items by 2025-07-25
action_items: Maya: send annotated pen-test spreadsheet + remediation tracker; due 2025-07-24
Diego: run targeted exploit repro on vulnerable endpoint (staging) and capture logs; due 2025-07-28
Tom: confirm patch window constraints and maintenance freeze dates; due 2025-07-29
Lena: create risk-acceptance doc for legacy telemetry service; due 2025-07-31
meeting_header: Date: 2025-07-22 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (CISO, Aegis), Tom Nguyen (Sr. DevOps), Lena Ortiz (Product Security), Marcus Hale (VP Eng)
summary: Redwood and Aegis reviewed the recent third-party penetration report and triaged findings into immediate remediation, patch-sprint candidates, and accepted risks. Conversation covered patch cadence constraints, secure SDLC touchpoints, KMS/encryption questions, audit-log retention, and a temporary mitigation playbook for high-risk vectored exploits.
topics: Penetration test highlights and severity breakdown
Vulnerability remediation timeline and sprint planning
Patch windows, maintenance freeze, and rollback considerations
Secure SDLC gaps identified (dependency scanning, backporting, RBAC reviews)
Encryption, KMS integration, and audit log retention policies
Interim mitigations and risk acceptance criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Well kick off, confirm audio/video, and then go straight into the pen test findings. I think we have about 50 minutes.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Audio's good, Maya. Thanks. Appreciate the quick turnaround on getting the report.
[00:18] Diego Ruiz: Quick intro -- Diego, security SE from Redwood, focusing on remediation patterns and patch automation.
[00:25] Marcus Hale: Marcus here, short intro from my side. We want a clear plan, low disruption, and to understand any showstoppers for prod.
[00:33] Tom Nguyen: Hi all. Im Tom, DevOps. Im most concerned about patch windows and any changes to our CI/CD pipelines.
[00:39] Lena Ortiz: Lena, product security. Im tracking the telemetry/legacy service findings.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Great. Ok jump to slide 3 in the shared report. High-level: vendor pen test ran late June, 78 findings, we triaged 12 high, 23 medium, rest low info. We annotated and proposed remediation categories.
[01:05] Priya Patel: The 12 high is what hit us. Can you call out the top three that you think need immediate attention?
[01:11] Diego Ruiz: Sure. Top three per our triage: 1) unauthenticated file upload leading to RCE on telemetry-ingest (CVE-like), 2) misconfigured S3 buckets exposing logs (data residency concern), 3) weak KMS key rotation policy allowing long-lived keys and lack of envelope encryption on backups.
[01:33] Tom Nguyen: For the RCE, that's the telemetry legacy endpoint that lives on a 2.x runtime we haven't upgraded cause of compat issues. We need a plan to backport patches or apply WAF rules.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Yes -- we recommended an immediate WAF rule as a temporary mitigation plus a hotfix patch. Diego, you had notes on repro?
[01:52] Diego Ruiz: I do. Ill run a targeted exploit repro in staging to validate the exact payload and surface logs — that will help prioritize whether it's exploitable in prod. Thats action item for me.
[02:05] [02:05] Lena Ortiz: Also, if you look at finding 7, the telemetry service uses a deprecated dependency with a known CVE that requires coordinated backporting across three microservices. That's probably why we have the exposure.
[02:20] Marcus Hale: Is this a blocker for our compliance attestation, Priya?
[02:24] Priya Patel: Not automatically a blocker but we have to show a remediation timeline and compensating controls for SOC 2 and our ISO audit next quarter. Audit wants proof of mitigations or a documented risk-acceptance for legacy systems.
[02:36] Maya Chen: On the S3 bucket findings, our recommendation is to rotate keys, apply least-privilege policies, enable object lock and then run a permissions re-audit. For data residency concerns, if the buckets are in the wrong region we propose rehosting the buckets and setting up cross-region replication if needed.
[02:53] Tom Nguyen: We do have some buckets sitting in eu-west but tagged incorrectly from an old project. We'll need time to move data without downtime. Typical maintenance window policy might require 2 weeks notice.
[03:05] Diego Ruiz: Another practical step is to enable server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS and ensure S3 bucket policies only allow access from our VPC endpoints. That buys time while you plan migration.
[03:18] Priya Patel: Can Redwood integrate with our KMS? We use an HSM-backed KMS with key access control.
[03:24] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and brings audit logs to the control plane. But if youre on hosted today, we can do envelope encryption with customer-supplied keys via an integration. Diego can share the config spec.
[03:36] Diego Ruiz: Ill attach the KMS config template to the annotated spreadsheet. Theres a known limitation on rotations for backups that we called out -- you need to run a re-encrypt step for existing snapshots.
[03:48] [03:48] Marcus Hale: About audit logs -- the pen test flagged missing retention rules for logs in one account. How does Redwood surface logs and retention?
[03:55] Maya Chen: In Redwood Console we expose per-route audit logs, with retention tiers. You can set retention policy per-tenant and export to your archive (S3/GCS). For Private deployments, the logs remain in your VPC and we can push to your SIEM.
[04:10] Lena Ortiz: Important for us: legal needs 7 years for certain telemetry archives for regulatory reasons. Can Redwood support that retention?
[04:17] Diego Ruiz: Yes, retention is configurable; long-term retention hits cost but we can tier hot/cold storage. We recommend exporting infrequent access logs to your archive.
[04:26] Priya Patel: On RBAC and SSO -- pen test found excessive privileges on a service account used by CI. Wed like to see role scoping and MFA enforced for high privilege roles.
[04:35] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SSO via SAML/SCIM and RBAC scopes. You can map groups to roles and require MFA at IdP level. We also have token rotation builtin for service tokens.
[04:44] Tom Nguyen: Our CI uses a service token with broad scopes currently. How hard is it to narrow to per-route tokens?
[04:49] Diego Ruiz: Not hard. Weve got suggestions for moving to least-privilege deploy tokens and short-lived certificates via your IdP. It does require pipeline changes but its a common pattern.
[04:59] [04:59] Priya Patel: I want to talk about secure SDLC gaps—there were notes on missing dependency scanning and no backport policy. Whats the recommended cadence?
[05:07] Maya Chen: We recommend integrating SCA (software composition analysis) in pipeline, weekly dependency vulnerability scans, and a quarterly backport policy for LTS runtimes. Also flagging high severity CVEs for immediate patch sprints.
[05:20] Marcus Hale: How do you recommend we schedule patch sprints so we dont break feature delivery?
[05:25] Diego Ruiz: Two options: 1) dedicated patch sprints (1-2 weeks) every quarter for medium/low, with hotfix lanes for critical/high; or 2) weekly micro-patches with CI gating and canary deploys. Many customers run a hybrid: weekly small patches + quarterly hardening sprint.
[05:40] Tom Nguyen: Our constraints: we have a release freeze around month end for regulatory reporting. So the patch plan needs to respect that.
[05:47] Maya Chen: Noted. Action item: Tom to confirm freeze windows and maintenance policy.
[05:52] [05:52] Lena Ortiz: On the misconfigured S3, well need a rollback plan in case of permission changes. Past ops changed policies and caused job failures.
[06:01] Diego Ruiz: Add a policy change canary: apply the least-privilege policy to a subset of objects and run lambda-based unit checks. We'll share a sample script.
[06:11] [06:11] Priya Patel: Regarding risk acceptance: the pen test called one medium issue acceptable because its behind additional controls. We need language for auditors.
[06:20] Maya Chen: We can provide a formal compensating control write-up template that maps findings to controls (e.g., control CC6 for incident mgmt). Use that for SOC 2 narratives.
[06:29] Marcus Hale: Good. Next, encryption --- the report said backups lacked envelope encryption. Is that a process change or platform change?
[06:36] Diego Ruiz: Process plus platform. You need to enable CMKs for snapshots and rotate keys; also ensure backup tool re-encrypts existing snapshots. For platform, we can enable envelope encryption at the service layer if you choose Redwood Private.
[06:48] [06:48] Tom Nguyen: Any rough ETA to get the telemetry service patched and WAF rule in prod?
[06:54] Maya Chen: WAF rule could be applied within 24-48 hours as a temporary mitigation. Patch ETA depends on backport complexity — initial triage within 3 business days, patch in staging within 7-10 business days if backporting is straightforward.
[07:08] Diego Ruiz: Ill aim to reproduce in staging and confirm exploitability by July 28. If confirmed high risk, prioritize hotfix.
[07:16] [07:16] Priya Patel: For the S3 region mis-tagging, Tom, can ops do a phased migration?
[07:21] Tom Nguyen: Yes, we can do phased rehosting with cross-region replication and a cutover window. We need to communicate to compliance.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Ok, lets talk about communication to auditors: we recommend one consolidated remediation tracker for auditors that lists finding, severity, assigned owner, mitigation, ETA, evidence link. We will populate Redwoods annotations and send it.
[07:44] Lena Ortiz: Please include screenshots of WAF rule firing and staging logs as evidence.
[07:50] Diego Ruiz: We will capture sample logs and curl traces; note that transcribed payloads sometimes get normalized by our tools so we will indicate raw vs sanitized.
[07:59] [07:59] Marcus Hale: Any blockers from Redwood side if we want accelerated remediation?
[08:04] Maya Chen: None to accelerate -- we can provide engineering hours for Private onboarding or dedicated support for hotfixes under an SOW. For hosted customers, we can push patches through our release pipeline but need your CI access for token scoping changes.
[08:19] Tom Nguyen: On SSO and RBAC, is there a way to audit service token use on a per-route level?
[08:25] Diego Ruiz: Yes, per-route token metrics are available in Console. You can see token usage, last used timestamp, IP, and map it back to a service account. We also support token revocation hooks via webhook to your infra.
[08:40] [08:40] Priya Patel: We also want to see proof that key rotation happened in the past 12 months for KMS. Is there an audit view?
[08:46] Maya Chen: For Private or Dedicated setups we surface key rotation events and audit logs; for Hosted we can provide rotation timestamps and KMS event exports.
[08:55] Lena Ortiz: For the legacy telemetry, can we do a short-lived compensation control like network egress filtering and internal-only access while we patch?
[09:03] Diego Ruiz: Yes, restrict L4/L7 access to that service via security groups and VPC-only endpoints and add egress filtering; we'll supply a recommended security group template.
[09:12] [09:12] Maya Chen: Alright, lets run through the prioritized remediation backlog. Ill read the top five and well assign owners.
[09:18] Maya Chen: #1 Telemetry RCE (High) — temp WAF + backport patch. Owner: Diego/Tom.
[09:26] (overlap) Tom Nguyen: Confirmed.
[09:28] Maya Chen: #2 S3 bucket public exposure (High) — rotate credentials, tighten bucket policy, rehost if needed. Owner: Tom/Lena.
[09:36] Maya Chen: #3 KMS rotation gaps (High) — enable CMK and re-encrypt backups. Owner: Lena/Tom.
[09:45] Maya Chen: #4 CI service account scope (Medium) — scoping and token rotation to limited-route tokens. Owner: Tom.
[09:52] Maya Chen: #5 Dependency backporting (Medium) — create a backport plan for LTS runtime. Owner: Marcus/Lena.
[10:00] [10:00] Priya Patel: That assignment looks right. Can we get a readout template for auditors?
[10:05] Maya Chen: Yes, well send the template and fill first pass for you.
[10:09] Diego Ruiz: One more note: the pen-test included a proof-of-concept exploit that depends on an older cipher negotiation. A mitigation is to disable legacy ciphers on the ingress proxy — thats a low-friction change.
[10:20] Tom Nguyen: Well schedule that config change in the next maintenance window and run smoke tests.
[10:25] [10:25] Marcus Hale: Anything else on compliance posture we should be aware of?
[10:30] Priya Patel: We need to ensure our SOC 2 evidence set is updated with these mitigations and have a written risk acceptance for legacy telemetry if its not fully remediated by audits.
[10:41] Maya Chen: Well include a risk-acceptance template and recommended wording for auditors. Also include a timeline in the remediation tracker.
[10:49] [10:49] Diego Ruiz: Ill attach the sample WAF rule and a policy canary script in the tracker.
[10:54] Priya Patel: Good. Lets confirm next meeting date suggested?
[10:58] Maya Chen: Proposed follow-up 2025-08-05 for 60 minutes to review patch sprint plan and evidence. Anyone object?
[11:06] Tom Nguyen: Works for me.
[11:08] Marcus Hale: Works.
[11:10] Lena Ortiz: Works.
[11:12] Priya Patel: Works.
[11:14] Maya Chen: Great. Recap: Maya will send annotated spreadsheet and tracker by 2025-07-24; Diego will run repro in staging by 2025-07-28; Tom confirms maintenance freeze windows by 2025-07-29; Lena drafts risk-acceptance doc by 2025-07-31.
[11:31] (crosstalk)
[11:33] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, well follow up with links.
[11:35] Priya Patel: Thanks, bye.
[11:37] Diego Ruiz: Thanks all.
[11:40] [End of recording]
